title: Multi-region chaos harness: simulate concurrent region loss + GPU pool exhaustion + dependency blackholes
creator: Ayesha Malik
description:
Objective: build an automated chaos test harness for staging that exercises a realistic, high-risk failure combination: (1) sudden loss of a primary region, (2) near-simultaneous exhaustion of the primary GPU pool in the secondary region, and (3) network-level blackholes to critical dependencies (e.g., metadata service, Kubernetes API, feature-flag service).

Why: previous incidents showed that single-failure injection tests (region loss OR GPU pool pressure) pass individually, but concurrent degradations lead to cascading circuit-breaker trips and opaque load-shedding behavior that violates SLOs and leaves customer traffic in an unrecoverable state. We need reproducible end-to-end validation that: failover policies, shed priorities, and circuit-breaker thresholds result in graceful degradation rather than full outage.

Scope: harness targets staging cluster topology mirroring production routing (primary region + secondary region with cross-region fallback). The chaos driver will be able to: withdraw a region (simulate cloud region outage), mark GPU nodes unschedulable/exhausted, and inject TCP/HTTP blackholes for selected dependencies. Traffic generator will mimic real query mix (short chat, long completion, batching patterns). Observability assertions will validate SLO-related signals (p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost, circuit-breaker states, retry churn).
acceptance_criteria: Automated scenario run reproduces failure combination without manual intervention
When primary region is removed, 95% of prioritized traffic either (a) fails over within configured failover window or (b) is shed by policy with documented error codes and retry guidance
Circuit breakers in runtime and API gateway trip only for misbehaving services and do not cause neighbor-service cascade (validated by service-level metrics and traces)

GPU exhaustion in secondary region triggers configured load-shedding tiers (background/low-priority work trimmed first, critical requests preserved) and does not breach P99 latency SLO for critical route beyond agreed window
Dashboard panels and alerts added for test runs: automated smoke asserts on telemetry are green/fail as expected
Runbook and on-call playbook updated with clear remediation steps based on observed failure modes
A postmortem stub (template) auto-created on test failure to capture root cause hypotheses and next action items
tasks: Design scenario matrix (region failover timing, GPU exhaustion rate, dependency blackhole targets)
Implement chaos driver components: region-withdrawal, node-exhaustion (simulate 100% GPU saturation), dependency-blackhole (iptables/tcpdrop)
Create traffic generator profile from production trace sampling (short chat 40%, long-completion 30%, batch embeddings 20%, control 10%)
Integrate with CI: create pipeline job that runs harness in staging and posts summary to #reliability-tests channel
Add observability checks: SLO smoke tests, circuit-breaker state timeline, retry storms, token cost deltas
Author runbook and update on-call playbook with clear escalation for triple-failure cases
Coordinate a scheduled canary with SRE and Product for a controlled weekend run
Write end-to-end test that asserts graceful degradation semantics and non-regression for previously broken paths
